title: Handy's Louisiana Shakers
summary: Joins John Handy's ten-piece band and lists the players; aside about the Botley name.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, that was around about 1929 or 30 when it started. It started off. Then after I left them, then I started with Hande, John Hande. Yeah, remember who else?
Louisiana Shakers. Yeah, that was Louisiana Shakers.
Oh yeah. And he was the leader then?
Was he playing Faraday then or his alto?
No, he was still playing his alto.

Do you remember who else was in the band? The other? Well during that time they had Rickard on the trumpet, Alexis Rickard, Willie Paggio and Dukangi that was playing the trumpet. Morris French was playing trombone.
Did he use more than one cover? It was a big band? Yeah, it was a big band.
Yeah, big band. They had ten pieces.
And Morris French was on the trombone, Roy Evans was on the drums, Old Man Kimball was on the bass, and Hande was on the sax, George Clark and Edward Botley, and myself on the band.
It was two good siblings, George Clark and Edward Botley was talking about.
Oh, speaking of Botley, the old timers tell about this. Buddy Botley used to go up in the airplane, I mean in the balloon.
No, this was a little younger. No relation at all. No relation. No relation.
He lived over on the Gravier of Perdido along in that section, near the old Simon Call along in there. So I just wondered, no relation. No relation.
